events.text: Meanings could thus be "The Assembly of Death/the Dead", referring to public executions on the plaza around 1050 CE; "The Mosque at the End of the World"; or a reference to a mosque with a distinctive courtyard or square in front of it.
Marrakesh was founded by the Almoravid dynasty in 1070 by Abu Bakr ibn Umar and subsequently developed by his successors.
events.section: Early history: Almoravid and Almohad periods

events.text: The Almoravid emir Ali ibn Yusuf (ruled 1106–1143) soon afterwards constructed a palace directly south of and adjacent to the Ksar el-Hajjar, on the actual site of the later Kutubiyya Mosque.
events.section: Early history: Almoravid and Almohad periods

events.text: After a destructive struggle, Marrakech fell to the Almohads in 1147, who undertook many construction projects throughout the city.
events.section: Early history: Almoravid and Almohad periods

events.text: Notably, a new royal kasbah (citadel) was erected further south by Ya'qub al-Mansur after 1184.
events.section: Early history: Almoravid and Almohad periods

events.label: 19th c.
events.text: The ruined outline of its walls was apparently still visible in the 19th century and corresponded roughly to the current site of the "Souk Jdid" (the "new souk" just north of the food-stalls).
On January 24, 1864, a massive explosion took place in the area of the square, reportedly caused by the criminal negligence of certain officials trying to avoid a government inspection.
events.section: Later history: Saadian period to modern times

events.text: In 1922 the government (under French administration at the time), passed the first laws aimed at protecting and preserving the square's cultural space and heritage.
events.section: Later history: Saadian period to modern times

events.text: In 2001 the square was proclaimed an Intangible Cultural Heritage by UNESCO, and in 2008 it was included in UNESCO's List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
events.section: Later history: Saadian period to modern times

events.text: Shortly before noon on April 28, 2011, a blast originating in a café in the square killed 17 people and injured another 25.
An earthquake with a 6.8 magnitude that struck Morocco in the evening of Friday the 8th of September 2023 highly damaged the Kharbouch Mosque and collapsed its minaret, which overlooked the square.
Beginning in May 2025, the square underwent a major renovation program scheduled for completion by the end of the year.
events.section: Later history: Saadian period to modern times

intro: Jemaa el-Fnaa (Arabic: ساحة جامع الفناء, romanized: Sāḥat Jāmiʿ al-Fanāʾ; Standard Moroccan Tamazight: ⵊⴰⵎⵄ ⵍⴼⵏⴰ, romanized: Jamɛ Lfna), also Jemaa el-Fna, Djema el-Fna or Djemaa el-Fnaa, is a square and market place in the medina quarter (old city) of Marrakesh, Morocco. It remains the main square of Marrakesh, used by locals and tourists.
